content: 1. Jolliffe J, Noorani H, Rees K, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the effectiveness of exercise-based rehabilitation for patients with coronary heart disease. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Medicine in 2004, volume 116, pages 682–692. 2. Taylor RS, Sagar VA, Davies EJ, Briscoe S, Coats AJ, Dalal H, et al. performed a Cochrane systematic review in 2014 (Cochrane Database Systematic Review, issue 4, article CD003331) to assess the impact of exercise-based rehabilitation on patients with heart failure. 3. Wells KB, Jones L, Chung B, Dixon EL, Tang L, Gilmore J, et al. conducted a community-partnered, cluster-randomized comparative effectiveness trial to examine the outcomes of community engagement and planning versus resource-based services in addressing depression disparities. This study was published in the Journal of General Internal Medicine in 2013, volume 28, pages 1268–1278. 4. Burns T, Knapp M, Catty J, Healey A, Henderson J, Watt H, et al. performed a systematic review on the effectiveness of home treatment for mental health problems. Their findings were published in Health Technology Assessment in 2001, volume 5, pages 1–139. 5. Caplan GA, Coconis J, Board N, Sayers A, Woods J. conducted a randomized controlled trial (the REACH-OUT trial) to determine whether home treatment impacts the incidence of delirium in elderly patients. The study compared rehabilitation and care at home with usual treatment and was published in Age and Ageing in 2006, volume 35, pages 53–60. 6. Beswick AD, Rees K, Dieppe P, Ayis S, Gooberman-Hill R, Horwood J, et al. carried out a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate complex interventions aimed at improving physical function and maintaining independent living in elderly individuals. Their work was published in The Lancet in 2008, volume 371, pages 725–735. 7. Dixon S, Nancarrow SA, Enderby PM, Moran AM, Parker SG. utilized a discrete choice experiment to assess patient preferences for different community-based care delivery models. Their findings were published in Health Expectations in 2015, volume 18, pages 1204–1214. 8. Gilbertson L, Langhorne P. investigated the satisfaction of stroke patients with home-based occupational therapy, focusing on occupational performance and service provision. Their study was published in the British Journal of Occupational Therapy in 2000, volume 63, pages 464–468. 9. Henderson C, Phelan M, Loftus L, Dall’Agnola R, Ruggeri M. compared patient satisfaction with community-based psychiatric services versus hospital-based psychiatric services. Their findings were published in Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica in 1999, volume 99, pages 188–195. 10. Jester R, Hicks C. conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis comparing hospital-at-home interventions with inpatient care. Their findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Nursing in 2003, volume 12, pages 20–27. 11. Families of adults with severe mental illness were surveyed to assess their satisfaction with inpatient and outpatient treatment. The results were published in the Psychosocial Rehabilitation Journal in 1992, volume 16, pages 121–134. 12. Utens CM, Goossens LM, van Schayck OC, Rutten-van Molken MP, van Litsenburg W, Janssen A, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate patient preferences and satisfaction with hospital-at-home care versus usual hospital care for COPD exacerbations. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Nursing Studies in 2013, volume 50, pages 1537–1549. 13. Chatterjee S, Pillai A, Jain S, Cohen A, Patel V. examined the outcomes of individuals with psychotic disorders participating in a community-based rehabilitation program in rural India. Their study was published in the British Journal of Psychiatry in 2009, volume 195, pages 433–439. 14. Court H, Ryan B, Bunce C, Margrain TH. evaluated the effectiveness of the new community-based Welsh low vision service. Their findings were published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology in 2011, volume 95, pages 178–184. 15. Copolillo A, Ivanoff SD. explored the use of assistive technology and home modifications for individuals with neurovisual deficits. Their study was published in Neurorehabilitation in 2011, volume 28, pages 211–220. 16. Wolfe DL, Hseih JTC, Mehta S. reviewed rehabilitation practices and associated outcomes following spinal cord injury. This work was part of the SCIRE Project, published in Vancouver, BC, in 2012. 17. Mossialos E, Dixon A. provided an introduction to health care funding in their book chapter, Funding health care: options for Europe, published by Open University Press in 2002, pages 1–30. 18. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report in 2016 titled Health financing for universal coverage, which defines the concept of universal health coverage and its implications. 19. Harvey RL, Roth EJ, Heinemann AW, Lovell LL, McGuire JR, Diaz S. investigated clinical predictors of resource utilization in stroke rehabilitation. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 1998, volume 79, pages 1349–1355. 20. Brusco NK, Taylor NF, Watts JJ, Shields N. conducted an economic evaluation of adult rehabilitation across various settings through a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2014, volume 95, pages 94–116. 21. Green A, Ali B, Ross D. examined resource allocation and budgetary mechanisms in decentralized health systems, using experiences from Baluchistan, Pakistan. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2000, volume 78, pages 1024–1035. 22. Puhan MA, Gimeno-Santos E, Scharplatz M, Troosters T, Walters EH, Steurer J. conducted a Cochrane systematic review on pulmonary rehabilitation following exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Their findings were published in 2011 (Cochrane Database Systematic Review, article CD005305). 23. Ayanian JZ, Weissman JS, Schneider EC, Ginsburg JA, Zaslavsky AM. investigated the unmet health needs of uninsured adults in the United States. Their findings were published in JAMA in 2000, volume 284, pages 2061–2069. 24. Iezzoni LI, Frakt AB, Pizer SD. highlighted the substantial barriers to health care services faced by uninsured individuals with disabilities. Their study was published in the Disability and Health Journal in 2011, volume 4, pages 238–244. 25. Ross JS, Bradley EH, Busch SH. analyzed the use of health care services by uninsured adults with lower and higher incomes. Their findings were published in JAMA in 2006, volume 295, pages 2027–2036. 26. Kogan MD, Newacheck PW, Blumberg SJ, Ghandour RM, Singh GK, Strickland BB, et al. examined underinsurance among children in the United States. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2010, volume 363, pages 841–851. 27. Skinner AC, Mayer ML. conducted a systematic review of the literature to assess the effects of insurance status on children’s access to specialty care. Their findings were published in BMC Health Services Research in 2007, volume 7, article 194. 28. Buchanan R, Radin D, Chakravorty BJ, Tyry T. explored the perceptions of informal caregivers regarding health and support services provided to individuals with multiple sclerosis. Their study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation in 2010, volume 32, pages 500–510. 29. Jeffrey AE, Newacheck PW. synthesized evidence on the role of insurance for children with special health care needs. Their findings were published in Pediatrics in 2006, volume 118, pages e1027–e1038. 30. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report in 2016 on global cooperation in assistive technology, emphasizing its importance for individuals with disabilities. 31. Borg J, Khasnabis C, editors. developed guidelines on the provision of manual wheelchairs in resource-limited settings. This report was published by the World Health Organization in 2008. 32. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report in 2008 titled Scaling up health services: challenges and choices, addressing the complexities of expanding health care services globally. 33. The World Health Organization (WHO) introduced the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health in 2001, providing a standardized framework for understanding and measuring health and disability. 34. Waddington C, Egger D. authored a technical brief for the WHO in 2008 titled Integrated health services – what and why? which explores the rationale and implementation of integrated health care systems.
